To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed fully deformable organic nanowire transistors, which are impervious even to large 3D volume change (1700% expansion and reverting back) of soft matter surfaces.
we report a deformable field‐effects transistor that can be attached on a mechanically dynamic surface and operate with constant current output.
we have developed fully deformable field‐effects transistors (Deformable FETs) that are imperviable to mechanical influences when mounted on dynamically changing soft matters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of organic semiconductor nanowires (OSNW) for use in flexible electronics.
a new class of organic nanowire transistors that are mechanically deformable, and thus, they are suitable for applications on surfaces of soft matters.
the design and synthesis of novel conjugated polymers for the development of new electronic materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have demonstrated that the organic semiconducting NWs can be made deformable and mechanically robust, which can be applied to the next‐generation implant devices.
we have demonstrated a novel concept of a single NW‐based FET that is fully deformable on dynamically deforming soft matter surfaces, and can withstand 3D volumetric changes of 1700%.
the authors have successfully demonstrated the first deformable organic nanowire FETs, which can be used in next‐generation implantables and soft electronics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a fully deformable organic nanowire FETs can be achieved by the use of a high-molecular-weight polyethylene oxide as the molecular binder and mechanical deformability enhancer, which can be applied to a dynamically changing surface, e.g. the beating heart, without any electrical performance degradation.

we have successfully demonstrated a new type of fully flexible organic nanowire field‐effect transists that are imperviously deformable to large mechanical deformations, which are of great potential for next-generation implantable bioelectronics.
we developed a new concept for deformable transistor by using single nanowire as the semiconductor.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of single organic NWs as semiconductors for deformable FETs is a simple yet effective approach to achieve high‐performance and reliable electronic devices that can withstand mechanical deformations on the surface of soft materials, such as human tissues.
the mechanical durability of organic NW FETs can be enhanced by the use of molecular binders that are capable of withstanding large deformations.
organic NW FETs are mechanically deformable and robust enough to withstand mechanical deformation on a soft surface.
